topic.title: FujiNet in AltirraSDL
topic.p: FujiNet is an add-on for Atari 8-bit computers. A real FujiNet plugs into the Atari's disk drive (SIO) port and uses Wi-Fi to load games and programs from servers on the internet. It can also act as a printer, modem, clock and network adapter for software written to use it.

You do not need to own a FujiNet. FujiNet-PC is a free program that does the same job on your computer, and AltirraSDL can start it for you. AltirraSDL talks to FujiNet over the network using a protocol called NetSIO, so FujiNet-PC, a real FujiNet device and AltirraSDL can all run on different machines if you want.

First complete setup in Tools > FujiNet. The welcome page shows setup and connection choices. Once FujiNet-PC is configured, Use FujiNet offers two shortcuts, and Setup and full controls collapses the setup instructions. Expand it whenever you want to change setup or use the other boot and file tools.

ul.li: Network games / Lobby opens the official FujiNet Game Lobby on the Atari. Enter a player name on first use, then choose a game and room. This uses FujiNet's multiplayer services; AltirraSDL's Netplay lobby is a separate feature.

BBS directory opens the official FujiNet Atari BBS Client, which loads an online directory of ATASCII boards. Choose a board and press Return. SELECT opens local controls; OPTION disconnects. You do not need to configure a modem driver or baud rate.

topic.p: Each shortcut starts the configured FujiNet-PC if needed, waits for its connection, downloads the Atari client, mounts it read-only and boots it through FujiNet. During launch the activity buttons are replaced by progress and Cancel activity. BASIC is unchanged, and local disk images and unsaved disk changes are kept. The Atari restarts when the client is ready to boot.

These clients need an Atari computer with at least 48 KB RAM. Remove inserted cartridges and disable any full-drive emulator on D1 before launching. These shortcuts use the FujiNet-PC managed by AltirraSDL on This computer. For another FujiNet, use its CONFIG menu: L opens the game lobby; current CONFIG versions also offer G for BBS.
topic.h2: Set up FujiNet in one click

ol.li: Open Tools > FujiNet. The first time, it opens on a welcome page.

topic.p: AltirraSDL then finds the newest official FujiNet-PC for your computer on FujiNet's GitHub page, downloads it (a few megabytes), checks it against its published SHA-256 checksum, installs it in AltirraSDL's own settings folder (FujiNet-PC), starts it and restarts the Atari. A fresh FujiNet configuration boots its menu, called CONFIG. A checklist shows each step. Nothing is installed system-wide, and your disk images and settings are kept. If the usual network port is already used by another program, such as a second AltirraSDL window, the next free port is chosen automatically. On later visits, choose an activity to start the installed copy, or expand Setup and full controls for the other startup and boot actions.

To start FujiNet with the emulator, expand Setup and full controls and turn on Start FujiNet when AltirraSDL starts. AltirraSDL then starts FujiNet-PC and boots the Atari using FujiNet's current boot configuration and mounted disks. Opening a program from the command line, for example by double-clicking a disk image, skips this so your program runs. In Gaming Mode FujiNet-PC starts without restarting the Atari behind the Game Library.

On a Mac, FujiNet-PC needs the OpenSSL library from Homebrew, which cannot be installed without your password. If it is missing, the checklist says so and offers Install in Terminal: Terminal opens with the command ready (it installs Homebrew first if needed). When Terminal says it has finished, select Check again and setup continues by itself.

A dropped or stalled download is retried automatically. If the download is still not possible (no internet, or GitHub is temporarily limiting requests), the checklist explains why and offers Try again or Download FujiNet-PC yourself instead. To get a newer FujiNet-PC later, open FujiNet-PC program in the full controls and select Install latest FujiNet-PC; your FujiNet settings, server list and SD card are kept.

The welcome page also offers I already downloaded FujiNet-PC and I have a FujiNet device or run FujiNet-PC myself. Full controls shows every option. After managed setup, the panel leads with Lobby and BBS; expand Setup and full controls to reach the two connection tabs:

ul.li: This computer (recommended): AltirraSDL starts and stops FujiNet-PC for you. No hardware needed.
Other FujiNet: a real FujiNet device on your network, or a FujiNet-PC that you start and manage yourself. AltirraSDL opens a connection and waits for FujiNet to connect to it.

topic.h2: Which file do I download myself?
topic.p: Only needed if you do not use the automatic setup. The FujiNet download page lists dozens of files for many computers. The panel tells you the exact file for your system. You need the newest release named FujiNet-PC Nightly, and in it the file whose name starts with fujinet-pc-ATARI_ and ends with your system:

tr.td: Linux, 64-bit Intel/AMD, recent (glibc 2.38+, e.g. Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 39+)
Linux, 64-bit ARM, glibc 2.38+ (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04, Raspberry Pi OS based on Debian 13)
Mac with Apple Silicon, macOS 15 or newer
Mac with Intel processor, macOS 15 or newer

topic.p: Files for ADAM, APPLE, COCO, LYNX or RS232 are for other computers. The files named fujinet-ATARI-v1.x.zip or fujinet-ATARI-8mb-v1.x.zip in the regular numbered releases are firmware for the physical FujiNet device: when unpacked they contain only firmware.bin, bootloader.bin and similar files, and no program your computer can run. The panel recognizes this mistake and says so.

Mac only, one-time step: the Mac builds need OpenSSL from Homebrew. Install Homebrew from brew.sh, then type brew install openssl@4 in Terminal for the macOS 15 Apple Silicon build, or brew install openssl@3 for the macOS 14 and Intel builds. If macOS refuses to run the program because it was downloaded from the internet, run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine followed by the extracted folder in Terminal.
topic.h2: Set up a downloaded FujiNet-PC yourself

ol.li: Open Full controls (or expand Setup and full controls after setup). In This computer, select Download FujiNet-PC and download the file named in the panel.
Extract (unzip) the downloaded file into a folder you will keep, for example Documents/FujiNet-PC. It creates a folder called fujinet-pc-ATARI.

Select Choose FujiNet-PC and pick the program named fujinet (fujinet.exe on Windows) inside that folder. Do not pick run-fujinet; AltirraSDL already does what that script does. Keep the data folder next to the program.
Select Start and Boot FujiNet. AltirraSDL starts FujiNet-PC in the background, waits for it to connect, then restarts the emulated Atari using FujiNet's current boot configuration and mounted disks.

topic.p: Start without booting starts FujiNet-PC but leaves the Atari as it is; use Boot Atari later. Open Web Interface opens FujiNet's own settings page in your browser, where you can mount disks and edit the server list. Stop FujiNet-PC stops the program; closing AltirraSDL also stops it. FujiNet-PC sometimes restarts itself after a settings change; AltirraSDL handles that automatically.

AltirraSDL keeps FujiNet-PC's settings, log and virtual SD card in its own FujiNet folder below the AltirraSDL configuration directory (Diagnostics > Open Data Folder). The extracted download is never modified, and your server list survives restarts and FujiNet-PC updates. To update FujiNet-PC, extract the newer download and choose its fujinet program with Change....
FujiNet-PC uses this computer's internet connection. Wi-Fi network names and passwords shown in FujiNet's menus only matter for a physical device.

ol.li: When the Atari shows CONFIG's HOST LIST, pick a server with the arrow keys (or 1-8) and press Return. fujinet.online, apps.irata.online and fujinet.diller.org are good places to start; their folders change over time. To add a server, select an empty slot, press E, type its name and press Return.
Browse folders with the arrow keys and Return. Pick a program ending in .XEX or a disk image ending in .ATR and press Return. Escape returns to the server list; Backspace goes up one folder.
When asked for a drive slot, choose 1 and press Return, then Return again for read-only. Choose write mode only for a disk image that you own and want to change.
Press Atari OPTION to start it. OPTION is F4 on your keyboard unless you changed the key mapping. The bottom line of the CONFIG screen lists the keys it accepts.

topic.p: Normal .XEX programs run directly; you do not need to convert them or boot DOS first. Programs written for a particular DOS or extra hardware still need that setup. Many games need BASIC off: if one does not start, turn off System > Internal BASIC (Boot Without Option Key) and select Boot Atari again. Leave BASIC on for BASIC programs.
CONFIG also offers L for FujiNet's Game Lobby. Network play needs games written for FujiNet; adding FujiNet does not make other games playable online.
topic.h2: Run a game file from this computer or a web link
topic.p: While FujiNet-PC runs on this computer and is connected, expand Setup and full controls and choose Run a file through FujiNet.... Select Choose local game..., or paste a direct HTTP(S) link and choose Download, mount and boot. AltirraSDL copies the game to FujiNet-PC's virtual SD card, puts it in drive 1 read-only through FujiNet's own interface, checks it, then boots the Atari from it through FujiNet.

It accepts single XEX/COM/EXE/OBX programs and ATR/ATX disk images up to 64 MiB. Use Game Library for ZIP collections. The Internal BASIC box changes the current profile's existing setting. Cancel file operation prevents the automatic boot; if mounting had already begun, check the web interface because FujiNet may have completed it. Changing profile or connection also cancels the automatic boot. This shortcut needs FujiNet-PC started by AltirraSDL; with Other FujiNet use CONFIG or the device's web page.
topic.h2: Copy your own games to the virtual SD card

ol.li: Download a program from its author or another source you trust.
Open Diagnostics > Open Data Folder and copy the file into its SD folder. This private SD card is separate from the SD folder in the extracted download, which is only copied once on first use.
In CONFIG choose the SD server, select the file, put it in drive 1 read-only and press OPTION.

topic.h2: Connect a real FujiNet device or your own FujiNet-PC

ol.li: Choose Other FujiNet, then Open connection. AltirraSDL now waits; FujiNet makes the connection.

In FujiNet's settings (its web page, or the [BOIP] section of FujiNet-PC's fnconfig.ini), turn on SIO over network (NetSIO, also called BOIP) and enter the host and port shown in the panel. For a FujiNet-PC on the same computer the host is 127.0.0.1 and the port normally 9997.

For a real FujiNet device or another computer, open Connection settings, turn on Allow other devices on my network to connect and select Apply connection settings. Enter this computer's IP address in FujiNet, and allow the UDP port in this computer's firewall.
When the panel says Connected, select Boot Atari. To use Open Web Interface, enter your FujiNet's web page address in Connection settings.

topic.p: Close connection stops accepting FujiNet traffic and Reopen connection resumes it; neither resets the Atari. A FujiNet that is already connected is left alone: AltirraSDL will not start its own FujiNet-PC until you close that connection. Android can connect to another FujiNet; the browser version cannot accept NetSIO connections.

ul.li: Allow other devices on my network to connect: off accepts only programs on this computer (127.0.0.1). On accepts any device on your network.
Port (UDP): where AltirraSDL waits for FujiNet, normally 9997. FujiNet must use the same number. With FujiNet-PC on this computer, AltirraSDL sets FujiNet-PC's port for you.
Reply timeout (ms): how long the Atari waits for FujiNet's answer to each command. Keep 100 unless you have a reason to change it.

Web page port (under FujiNet-PC program): the preferred port of FujiNet-PC's settings page, normally 8000. If occupied, AltirraSDL selects and remembers a free local port automatically. Open Web Interface uses that selected port. It is separate from the NetSIO port.

topic.p: After managed setup, Repair automatic setup remains visible even when the setup details are collapsed. It stops FujiNet-PC, restores local connection defaults, selects free ports and starts the installed program again. Your server list, disk settings and virtual SD files are kept. The current Atari game is not rebooted; select an activity or Boot Atari when ready. Cancel repair or switching profiles prevents a delayed repair from applying to another session. External FujiNet and manual bridge settings are not reset.

If a file or activity reports HTTP 404, inspect the URL and the runtime log: another application may own that web port, or the runtime may lack the mount API. Updating FujiNet-PC does not resolve a port conflict. Web-server startup failures are reported even if NetSIO connects; use Repair automatic setup to try a free port again.

While FujiNet is in use it acts as the Atari's drive 1 (D1:). Booting through FujiNet therefore switches off the emulator's own D1, turns off Fast boot and selects normal speed, because network transfers need real time. Your D1 disk image and its unsaved changes stay inserted; Emulator drives > Use emulator's D1 again switches it back on. Drives D2 and up and BASIC are not changed, so you can keep local disk images in D2 and up. Do not give a local disk and a FujiNet disk the same drive number. A full-drive emulator attached to D1 must be turned off in Configure System first; the panel tells you if so.
Save states keep the emulator's settings but cannot rewind FujiNet's files or network connections. After loading a state, select Boot Atari or reconnect if FujiNet seems out of step.

If this profile already uses the published NetSIO custom device and its Python hub, the panel shows Manual FujiNet connection. Keep starting the hub and FujiNet-PC as before; the panel offers Boot Atari and an optional web address and does not change your custom device, filters or processes. Recognition follows the custom device actually loaded, including when hot reload is disabled.

Use one route per profile. The built-in connection is blocked while a manual bridge is recognized; if both are active, disconnect the built-in one before booting. To switch, remove the NetSIO custom device in Configure System > Devices and stop its hub. Separate profiles let you keep both setups. Partly recognized scripts produce a caution rather than an automatic change.

ul.li: "This is firmware for a physical FujiNet device": you downloaded fujinet-ATARI-v1.x.zip. Download the fujinet-pc-ATARI_ file from FujiNet-PC Nightly instead (see the table above).

FujiNet-PC exits straight away: the panel explains missing libraries when it can. Linux builds need OpenSSL 3 (package libssl3 or openssl-libs) and Expat, which most systems already have; if it says the build is too new, use the ubuntu-22.04 file. Mac builds need Homebrew's OpenSSL (see above). Otherwise read Diagnostics > Runtime log.

Automatic setup cannot download: check the internet connection and try again. If GitHub is limiting requests from your network, wait an hour or download FujiNet-PC yourself. On Linux, downloading uses the system's libcurl library.
"Could not open port": another program already uses the port, often a second AltirraSDL window or a NetSIO hub. Close it, or choose another port in Connection settings.
Waiting for FujiNet forever: check the host and port entered in FujiNet, Allow other devices for a real device, and the firewall. The web page port is a different number from the NetSIO port.

The Atari does not show FujiNet's menu: make sure the panel says Connected and fix any D1 full-drive warning. Boot Atari restarts using FujiNet's current boot configuration and mounted disks; it does not clear disks or force CONFIG. If a previous program boots again, review the drives and boot settings in Open Web Interface. Avoid Warp speed with network software.

Lobby and BBS buttons are missing: finish managed-runtime setup first. During setup the panel shows progress. These shortcuts use This computer; with Other FujiNet or a manual bridge, use CONFIG on that FujiNet. Once configured, expand Setup and full controls to reach setup and connection options.
An activity was cancelled after mounting began: automatic boot is cancelled, but FujiNet may already have mounted the client. Check the web interface before choosing what to boot next.
Secure (HTTPS) downloads fail: read the runtime log, keep all files from the download together, and check the computer's clock and internet access. Certificate checks are never disabled.
Settings are greyed out: stop FujiNet-PC first. FujiNet changes are also unavailable during an online play session.
